title: Throwing a small oil bottle
subtitle: Throwing a narrow-necked bottle form in stoneware for olive oil or infused oils
excerpt: A narrow-necked oil bottle is one of the most satisfying wheel-thrown forms: the wide shoulder narrows to a thin neck that fits a cork or rubber stopper, and the belly is wide enough to hold 250 ml comfortably. This pattern throws a small stoneware oil bottle with a pulled spout opening and specifies the throwing sequence for achieving a stable neck-to-shoulder transition.
sourceNotes: Oil bottle form is a classic utilitarian stoneware thrown form. Proportions, neck specification, and throwing sequence derived from studio ceramics functional ware practice.

glossaryTerms.definition: Working the clay mass until it runs true with no wobble at any speed: required before pulling walls.
The throwing technique for narrowing a wide cylinder into a neck by squeezing inward with both hands from outside as the wheel turns.
The correct drying stage for trimming a foot ring.
The first kiln firing, which hardens the clay body without maturing the glaze. Bisque makes the piece easier to handle during glazing.

content.text: This pattern requires a pottery wheel and kiln firing to cone 6 (approximately 1220 °C). Use a food-safe mid-fire glaze for oil bottles: confirm with the glaze supplier that the glaze is rated for food contact. Apply the glaze witness cone test on each firing to verify temperature.

The oil bottle is thrown as a wide cylinder first, then the neck is formed by collaring: squeezing inward from the outside with both hands. The collar sequence requires patience: the neck must be narrowed in three to four passes, not in a single squeeze. Rushing the collar collapses the neck or creates an S-curve that makes the bottle unstable.
Throwing sequence
Weigh out 700 g of smooth stoneware. Wedge and
centre
on the wheel bat. Open to 8 cm interior diameter.

Pull the walls upward in three passes to a cylinder 14 to 15 cm tall with walls 5 to 6 mm thick. The cylinder should be straight-sided: not flared: because the belly will be shaped by pushing outward from inside.

Belly out the lower two-thirds of the form: press outward from inside with a supporting hand on the outside. The maximum diameter should be at about the mid-point of the cylinder height: 12 to 13 cm exterior diameter. Above the belly, the walls return to vertical before the collar sequence begins.
Begin the
collar

: place both hands around the upper third of the cylinder. Fingers and thumbs pointing upward, sides of the index fingers making contact with the clay. Squeeze gently inward while moving hands upward slowly. The opening narrows. Repeat this movement three to four times, each time starting from slightly lower on the form.

After two collar passes, the neck opening should be around 5 cm. After three passes, 3 to 4 cm. The final neck should be 2.5 to 3 cm interior diameter: wide enough for a standard cork (size 16 to 18 cork).

Refine the neck: compress and smooth the final 3 to 4 cm of the neck with a wet thumb and forefinger. The rim should be even in thickness and slightly thickened outward: not knife-thin, which would be fragile.
Cut from the bat with a wire cutter. Allow to reach
leather-hard
before trimming a foot ring.
Bisque
fire to cone 06. Glaze and fire to cone 6.
Finished dimensions

Target after firing: 17 cm tall (accounting for approximately 12 percent shrinkage from wet to fired). Maximum belly diameter 11 cm. Neck diameter (interior) 2 to 2.5 cm. Capacity approximately 250 ml.

rows.problem: Neck collapses or goes oval during collaring
rows.cause: Collaring too fast; walls too thin at the neck before collaring
rows.fix: Do not collar in one pass. Keep the walls at the upper section slightly thicker than the belly before starting to collar. Rest the clay for five minutes between collar passes if it starts to soften.

rows.problem: Shoulder-to-neck join shows a crease or sharp step
rows.cause: Collar started too abruptly; outward-belly transition meets collar transition too close together
rows.fix: Leave a 3 to 4 cm section of straight vertical wall between the widest point of the belly and where collaring starts.

rows.problem: Bottom of form too heavy after throwing
rows.cause: Opening left too much clay in the floor; belly did not push outward enough
rows.fix: Trim more aggressively from the foot ring area. The base should be no more than 8 mm thick after trimming.
